question.text: Deepa discovers that her mutual fund account statement shows a different address than her current residence. What should she do?

answer.text: Report it to SEBI as a data breach
Update it only when she makes her next transaction
Ignore it — the address doesn't affect her investments

Submit an address change request through the appropriate channel — KRA (with KYC update form, PAN and documentary address proof) if her folio is KRA-compliant, or to the AMC/RTA ISC with self-attested address proof if it is a non-KYC folio

explanation.text: The Logic: An outdated address means important communications (CAS, tax documents, scheme notices) may not reach the investor. The route depends on KYC status. For a KRA-compliant folio, the fund will not register the address change directly; the investor must update the address through KRA using a KYC update form along with PAN, new address and documentary address proof. For non-KYC folios, the investor submits self-attested address proof and PAN at the AMC/RTA Investor Service Centre. The Trap: An incorrect address is not a SEBI data breach, but it cannot simply be left in place. Equally, going straight to the AMC/RTA misses the KRA path for KRA-compliant folios — the AMC/RTA cannot register the change directly in that case. Note: Source: NISM Series II-B (RTA Mutual Fund) workbook — KRA route for address changes on KRA-compliant folios; AMC/RTA ISC route for non-KYC folios.
